Judged against atlas/A8.contract.md: benjamini_hochberg '0 < q < 1', stepdown_rejections 'Needs 0 < alpha < 1', romano_wolf 'alpha outside (0, 1) raises', and integrity_report inherits both through 'benjamini_hochberg(one-sided p-values, q)' and 'romano_wolf(returns, alpha, ...)'. The test asks for ValueError at q = 1, alpha = 1 (stepdown), alpha in {0, 1} (romano_wolf and integrity_report) and q = 1 (integrity_report) with otherwise valid inputs (50 x 4 trial set, n_blocks 4, n_boot 20; a 40 x 3 differentials matrix), so it asks only for what the contract requires. Passes on the reference for seeds 0-49 (run_graders and 50 targeted runs), passes on my independent variant (which validates in a different order), and kills v01 (KILLED by this test on seed 0 in my mutate_graders run).

Judged against the contract: 'n_blocks is reduced to the largest even number <= min(n_blocks, T). Needs T >= 4, so that each CSCV half-sample has at least 2 periods'; with T = 4 and n_blocks 16 the reduced count is 4, one-period blocks, two-period halves, and the CSCV rule '(T - T mod S) / 2 >= 2' holds. The test builds a 4 x 3 normal matrix (T = 4), runs integrity_report(n_blocks=16, n_boot=20) and requires n_trials = 3 and pbo equal to probability_of_backtest_overfitting(r, 4).pbo. Independent check that nothing else can raise: a four-point sample has kurtosis >= skewness**2 + 1, so the variance bracket 1 - g3*SR + (g4 - 1)/4*SR**2 >= (1 - g3*SR/2)**2 > 0 except on a measure-zero set. Passes on the reference (seeds 0-49) and my variant; kills v02.

Judged against the contract: 'mean_block a finite number >= 1'; with probability 1/mean_block = 1 every step starts a new block, which is the iid bootstrap. The test requires 50 integer indices in 0..49 from stationary_bootstrap_indices(50, 1.0, rng) and a boolean mask of length 3 from romano_wolf(..., mean_block=1.0). Both follow from the contract for any draw order. Passes on the reference (seeds 0-49) and my variant (different draws); kills v03.

Judged against the contract: 'One-sided p-value of trial n: 1 - Phi(mean / (std(ddof=1) / sqrt(T)))'. The helper _skewed_columns builds three circular shifts of one standardized exp(1)**2 sample (mean 0, sd 1 with ddof=1) plus t/sqrt(40), so each column's t-statistic is exactly t: 1.60 gives p = 0.05480 (> 0.05) and 1.70 gives p = 0.04457 (< 0.05); BH at q = 0.05 with three equal p-values rejects all three or none. I recomputed the PSR-based tail 1 - PSR(x, 0) for these shapes at seeds 0, 1, 2, 17 and 49: 0.0009 / 0.1493 (seed 0), 0.0002 / 0.1543, 0.0096 / 0.1131, 0.0005 / 0.1434, 0.0006 / 0.1489, so a PSR-based p-value lands on the other side of 0.05 for both cases, as the test's comment says. Passes on the reference (seeds 0-49) and my variant; kills v04. Limit found: the test cannot tell sqrt(T) from sqrt(T - 1) in the standard error, because 1.60 and 1.70 stay on the same side of 0.05 under a 1.3% change (see grader-mutant-w01).

Judged against the contract: 'all C(S, S/2) splits' in itertools order and 'n_combinations'. S = 12 on a 120 x 4 matrix requires 924 logits equal to the definition (cscv_definition, an independent loop in the test file, tolerance 1e-10); S = 16 on a 32 x 3 matrix requires n_combinations = C(16, 8) = 12,870 and as many logits (I recomputed comb(12, 6) = 924 and comb(16, 8) = 12,870). mutants.description: m01_bh_step_down: Benjamini-Hochberg run step-down: stops at the first ordered p-value above its line instead of taking the largest passing k.
m02_bh_sorted_mask: Benjamini-Hochberg returns the rejection mask in sorted (rank) order instead of the input order.
m03_bh_strict_inequality: Benjamini-Hochberg uses a strict inequality p_(k) < kq/m, so a p-value exactly on its line is not rejected.
m04_kurtosis_excess: sample_kurtosis returns excess kurtosis m4/m2**2 - 3 (the scipy default) where the contract requires raw kurtosis.
m05_se_divides_by_n: Sharpe-ratio standard error divides the variance bracket by n instead of n - 1.
m06_se_kurtosis_minus_three: Sharpe-ratio standard error uses (kurtosis - 3)/4 in the bracket, mixing the excess-kurtosis form with raw kurtosis.
m07_dsr_population_variance: Deflated Sharpe ratio takes the population variance (ddof=0) of the trial Sharpe ratios instead of ddof=1.
m08_ems_one_trial_returns_zero: expected_max_sharpe at N = 1 returns 0.0 instead of sr_mean (forgets the shift when there is no selection).
m09_sb_no_wraparound: Stationary bootstrap never wraps around: a block that would run past the last period starts a new block instead of continuing at index 0.
m10_sb_geometric_parameter_inverted: Stationary bootstrap uses mean_block as the restart probability (1/p in place of p), so every step starts a new block.
m11_rw_resamples_columns_independently: Romano-Wolf resamples each strategy with its own bootstrap index vector, breaking the cross-sectional dependence.
m12_rw_not_studentized: Romano-Wolf is not studentized: it compares raw mean differentials with centred bootstrap means instead of t-statistics.
m13_stepdown_weak_inequality: Step-down rejects hypotheses with t_obs >= c instead of t_obs > c.
m14_stepdown_interpolated_quantile: Step-down critical value is np.quantile(maxima, 1 - alpha) with linear interpolation instead of the ceil((1-alpha)B)-th order statistic.
m15_stepdown_floor_rank: Step-down critical value uses the floor((1-alpha)B)-th order statistic instead of the ceil((1-alpha)B)-th.
m16_stepdown_single_step: Step-down never recomputes the critical value: one max-T critical value over all hypotheses (single-step test).
m17_pbo_strict_logit: PBO counts logits < 0 instead of logits <= 0, so a median out-of-sample rank is not counted as overfit.
m18_pbo_drops_newest_rows: CSCV drops the newest T mod S rows instead of the oldest.
m19_pbo_ignores_ties_in_rank: CSCV out-of-sample rank ignores ties (1 + #lower, a 'min' rank) instead of the average rank with +0.5 per tie.
m20_report_two_sided_pvalues: integrity_report feeds Benjamini-Hochberg two-sided p-values 2(1 - Phi(|t|)) instead of one-sided p-values for H0: mean <= 0.
m21_report_no_block_reduction: integrity_report passes n_blocks to CSCV unchanged instead of reducing it to the largest even number <= min(n_blocks, T).
n01_imports_scipy_for_the_normal_cdf: Uses scipy.stats.norm for the PSR's normal CDF, a dependency the A8 contract forbids (NumPy and the standard library only).
n02_pbo_accepts_one_period_halves: CSCV omits the half-sample rule: with (T - T mod S) / 2 < 2 it runs on one-period half-samples instead of raising ValueError.
n03_rw_tiny_constant_for_constant_resample: Romano-Wolf studentizes a constant resampled column by np.finfo(float).tiny instead of the column's sample standard deviation.
n04_rw_skips_constant_draws: Romano-Wolf discards every bootstrap draw in which a resampled column is constant, instead of studentizing it by the column's sample standard deviation.
n05_report_silent_nan_pbo_on_short_samples: integrity_report runs on fewer than 4 periods and reports pbo = nan instead of raising ValueError.
n06_sharpe_flattens_two_dimensional_input: Series validation flattens a two-dimensional input with ravel() instead of raising ValueError.
n07_rw_bootstrap_uses_full_sample_sd: Romano-Wolf studentizes every bootstrap draw by the full-sample standard deviation instead of the draw's own std(d*_k, ddof=1).
n08_rw_bootstrap_sd_default_ddof: Romano-Wolf computes the bootstrap draws' standard deviations with np.std's default ddof=0, while the observed statistics use ddof=1.
n09_pbo_metric_plain_ratio: CSCV's subsample Sharpe metric is plain mean / std, ignoring the contract's rule for a constant subsample (0.0 if its mean is 0, +-inf by the sign of the mean otherwise).
n10_sb_first_block_starts_at_zero: Stationary bootstrap starts the first block at index 0 instead of at a uniform random index.
n11_moments_skip_series_validation: sample_skewness and sample_kurtosis skip the series validation, so a two-dimensional or non-finite input returns a number instead of raising ValueError.

p01_sharpe_zero_variance_by_std_equality: sharpe_ratio detects zero variance with std(x, ddof=1) == 0 instead of all values equal, so a constant non-dyadic series returns a huge Sharpe ratio instead of raising ValueError.
p02_rw_accepts_a_constant_column: romano_wolf omits the constant-column check, so a column with all values equal is studentized by its (zero or tiny) standard deviation instead of raising ValueError.

p03_rw_constant_resample_by_std_equality: romano_wolf detects a constant resampled column with std(d*_k, ddof=1) == 0 instead of all values equal, so a constant non-dyadic resample is divided by a tiny floating-point standard deviation.

p04_cscv_constant_subsample_by_std_equality: CSCV's subsample metric detects a constant subsample with std == 0 instead of all values equal, so a constant non-dyadic subsample gets a huge finite Sharpe ratio instead of +-inf.
p05_cscv_floors_the_subsample_sd: CSCV floors the subsample standard deviation at 1e-12 to avoid dividing by zero, so a constant non-zero subsample gets a large finite metric instead of +-inf.

p06_moments_zero_variance_by_m2_equality: sample_skewness and sample_kurtosis detect zero variance with m2 == 0 instead of all values equal, so a constant non-dyadic series returns a meaningless number instead of raising ValueError.
p07_sb_accepts_mean_block_below_one: stationary_bootstrap_indices does not validate mean_block, so mean_block < 1 (a restart probability above one) returns indices instead of raising ValueError.

q01_moments_not_rescaled: sample_skewness and sample_kurtosis compute their moments on the raw series (only the Sharpe ratio is rescaled), so a fourth power overflows at 1e155 and a square underflows at 2**-1000.

q02_rw_one_scale_for_the_whole_matrix: romano_wolf rescales the whole differentials matrix by the one power of two of its largest absolute value instead of each column by its own, so a column far smaller than the largest underflows when squared.

q03_rw_reseeds_inside_the_loop: romano_wolf creates rng = np.random.default_rng(seed) inside the bootstrap loop, so every draw reuses the same index vector instead of drawing n_boot vectors in order from one generator.

q04_rw_vectorized_index_draws: romano_wolf draws all n_boot index vectors at once from one generator (vectorized) instead of calling stationary_bootstrap_indices(T, mean_block, rng) once per draw in order, as the contract now requires.
q05_cscv_constant_subsample_scores_zero: CSCV scores every constant subsample 0.0 (zero variance read as zero Sharpe ratio) instead of +-inf by the sign of its value.

q06_rw_constant_column_by_std_equality: romano_wolf detects a constant column of differentials with std(d_k, ddof=1) == 0 instead of all values equal, so a constant non-dyadic column is studentized by a tiny standard deviation instead of raising ValueError.
q07_sb_mean_block_nan_accepted: stationary_bootstrap_indices checks only mean_block < 1, so a NaN mean_block (every comparison False) passes and yields one block instead of raising ValueError.

q08_se_overflow_escapes: sharpe_ratio_std squares the Sharpe ratio with sharpe**2, so a huge Sharpe ratio raises OverflowError instead of the contract's ValueError for a variance bracket that overflows.
q09_rw_alpha_unchecked: romano_wolf does not validate alpha (it calls the step-down loop directly), so alpha outside (0, 1) returns decisions instead of raising ValueError.

q10_dsr_trial_variance_not_rescaled: deflated_sharpe_ratio takes np.var(trial_sharpes, ddof=1) on the raw values, so a variance beyond the largest float warns and returns instead of raising ValueError.

q11_rw_resample_in_column_scale: romano_wolf studentizes each resample in its column's scale (rescales the column once, not the resample), so a resample of values far smaller than its column's largest has a square that underflows and a zero standard deviation.

q12_cscv_subsample_in_column_scale: CSCV computes each subsample's Sharpe ratio in its configuration's full-sample scale (rescales each column once, not each subsample), so a subsample of values far smaller than the column's largest has a zero standard deviation.
q13_bh_accepts_nan_pvalues: benjamini_hochberg checks the p-value range with comparisons only, so a NaN p-value (every comparison False) passes and is never rejected instead of raising ValueError.
q14_psr_benchmark_nan_only: probabilistic_sharpe_ratio rejects only a NaN benchmark (math.isnan), so an infinite sr_benchmark returns 0.0 or 1.0 instead of raising ValueError.

r01_scale_by_largest_value_not_magnitude: The power-of-two rescaling takes its exponent from the largest value (x.max()) instead of the largest absolute value, so a series dominated by a large negative return overflows when it is 'rescaled'.

r02_rw_one_seed_per_draw: romano_wolf seeds a fresh generator for every bootstrap draw (np.random.default_rng([seed, b])) instead of drawing all n_boot index vectors in order from the single rng = np.random.default_rng(seed).

r03_cscv_constant_subsample_ignores_sign: CSCV scores every constant nonzero subsample +inf, ignoring its sign, so a configuration that loses the same amount every period looks like the best in-sample.
r04_rw_constant_resample_population_sd: romano_wolf studentizes a constant resampled column by the column's population standard deviation (np.std default ddof=0) instead of std(d_k, ddof=1).
r05_integer_check_by_int_cast: Integer arguments are checked with int(x) != x, so an infinite n_obs, n_trials, n_boot or n_blocks raises OverflowError instead of ValueError.
r06_ems_textbook_quantile: expected_max_sharpe evaluates the textbook Phi^-1(1 - 1/N), which is infinite once 1 - 1/N rounds to 1 (N beyond 2**53), instead of -Phi^-1(1/N).

r07_se_keeps_numpy_scalars: sharpe_ratio_std does arithmetic on its scalar arguments as given, so a NumPy float64 Sharpe ratio whose square overflows raises a RuntimeWarning instead of the contract's ValueError.
r08_trialset_truncates_selected: TrialSet casts selected and periods_per_year with int() before validating them, so a fractional selected silently picks the column below it.

r09_rw_centre_overflow_unguarded: romano_wolf re-expresses the column mean in the resample's scale without guarding the overflow, so a column spanning more than 2**1024 between its largest value and a resample's largest value warns instead of giving the contract's -inf statistic.

r10_integer_check_rejects_numpy_integers: Integer arguments are checked with isinstance(x, int), so a NumPy integer (np.int64 from np.argmax or an array element) is rejected with ValueError although the contract accepts NumPy numbers.
r11_psr_keeps_numpy_benchmark: probabilistic_sharpe_ratio subtracts a NumPy-scalar benchmark without converting it with float(), so an extreme np.float64 benchmark raises an overflow RuntimeWarning.

r12_se_n_obs_finite_not_integral: sharpe_ratio_std checks only that n_obs is finite and at least 2, not that it is an integer, so a fractional n_obs such as 2.5 returns a standard error instead of raising ValueError.

r13_trialset_periods_per_year_finite_not_integral: TrialSet checks only that periods_per_year is finite and at least 1, not that it is an integer, so 251.5 is silently truncated to 251 instead of raising ValueError.

s01_rw_float_seed_not_converted: romano_wolf validates seed as an integer but passes it to np.random.default_rng unconverted, so an integral float seed such as 7.0, which the contract accepts, raises TypeError.

s02_pbo_float_n_blocks_not_converted: probability_of_backtest_overfitting validates n_blocks as an integer but uses it unconverted, so an integral float n_blocks such as 8.0, which the contract accepts, raises TypeError (slice indices must be integers).
s03_integer_bound_inclusive: Integer arguments are bounded by magnitude at most 2**1000 instead of below 2**1000, so n_trials or n_obs equal to 2**1000 is accepted instead of raising ValueError.

s04_integer_bound_for_ints_only: The 2**1000 bound on integer arguments is applied to Python and NumPy integers only, so an integral float such as 1e305 is accepted as n_trials or n_obs instead of raising ValueError.

s05_zero_variance_by_ptp: Zero variance is tested with np.ptp(x) == 0, whose subtraction overflows with a RuntimeWarning for a series spanning more than the largest float, such as [1e308, -1e308, 5e307].

s06_scale_divides_by_power_of_two: The power-of-two rescaling divides by 2.0**e instead of calling np.ldexp, so a series whose largest absolute value is at least 2**1023 (about 9e307) overflows the divisor to inf with a RuntimeWarning.

s07_rw_studentization_unguarded: romano_wolf guards the overflow of the re-expressed column mean but not of the studentized difference, so a resample far smaller than its column warns (overflow in divide) instead of giving the contract's quiet +-inf statistic.

s08_report_pvalues_not_rescaled: integrity_report computes the trials' t-statistics for the BH p-values on the unscaled returns, so a trial set of tiny or huge returns (2**-600 or 2**600 times ordinary ones) underflows or overflows its variances and warns.
s09_report_romano_wolf_ignores_seed: integrity_report does not forward its seed, so its Romano-Wolf bootstrap is always drawn from np.random.default_rng(0) whatever seed the caller passes.
s10_report_romano_wolf_ignores_alpha: integrity_report does not forward alpha, so its Romano-Wolf rejections always use romano_wolf's default level 0.05 whatever alpha the caller passes.

s11_dsr_rejects_equal_trial_sharpes: deflated_sharpe_ratio applies the zero-variance rule of a return series to trial_sharpes, so equal trial Sharpe ratios (variance 0, so SR0 = 0) raise ValueError instead of giving the PSR against 0.
t01_report_bh_uses_alpha_not_q: integrity_report validates q but runs Benjamini-Hochberg at alpha, the StepM level, so bh_rejections ignore the caller's q.

t02_report_romano_wolf_ignores_mean_block: integrity_report does not forward mean_block, so its Romano-Wolf bootstrap always uses romano_wolf's default mean block length 10 whatever the caller passes.
t03_report_pvalues_population_sd: integrity_report computes the trials' t-statistics for the BH p-values with np.std's default ddof=0 instead of std(ddof=1).

t04_stepm_per_hypothesis_critical_values: Step-down uses each hypothesis's own bootstrap quantile (the ceil((1-alpha)B)-th smallest t*_bk of column k) instead of the quantile of the maximum over the active set, so it controls no family-wise error.
t05_cscv_interleaved_blocks: CSCV forms its S blocks by interleaving rows (block i holds rows i, i+S, i+2S, ...) instead of consecutive runs of periods.
t06_report_annualizes_by_periods: integrity_report annualizes the selected Sharpe ratio by multiplying by periods_per_year instead of its square root.
t07_sb_start_index_off_by_one: Stationary bootstrap draws block starts with rng.integers(0, n - 1), an exclusive upper bound one too low, so the last period never starts a block.
t08_ems_hard_coded_forty_trial_bracket: expected_max_sharpe hard-codes Lesson 7 Example 3.2's bracket 2.1895 for N = 40 trials instead of evaluating the formula at the given N.
t09_dsr_ignores_n_trials: deflated_sharpe_ratio ignores an explicit n_trials and always deflates by len(trial_sharpes).
t10_psr_sign_reversed: probabilistic_sharpe_ratio subtracts in the wrong order, Phi((SR* - SR)/se), so it returns one minus the PSR.

u01_report_analyses_the_highest_sharpe_trial_not_the_selected_one: integrity_report ignores TrialSet.selected and reports on the trial with the highest Sharpe ratio, which is only the proposed strategy when the proposal is the in-sample best.

u02_stepdown_masks_rejected_hypotheses_in_the_callers_array: stepdown_rejections removes each rejected hypothesis from the maximum by writing -inf into its column of the caller's t_boot, so the caller's bootstrap matrix is mutated.
u03_cscv_in_sample_tie_goes_to_the_last_maximal_configuration: CSCV breaks an in-sample tie for the best configuration in favour of the highest index instead of the lowest.
u04_report_prints_a_summary_line: integrity_report prints a one-line summary of its result, a leftover debugging statement the contract forbids.

u05_romano_wolf_rescales_the_callers_matrix_in_place: romano_wolf multiplies the caller's differentials matrix by its per-column power of two in place, so the caller's data change although every decision stays the same.

u06_bh_sorts_the_callers_pvalues_in_place: benjamini_hochberg sorts the caller's p-value array in place after taking its ordering, so the caller's array is mutated although the returned mask is right.
u07_report_annualizes_with_252_whatever_the_periods_per_year: integrity_report annualizes the selected Sharpe ratio with a hard-coded sqrt(252), ignoring the trial set's periods_per_year.
u08_from_backtest_ignores_the_backtests_selected_column: TrialSet.from_backtest takes the in-sample best column as selected instead of the backtest result's own selected attribute.
v01_levels_accept_one: benjamini_hochberg, stepdown_rejections and romano_wolf accept a level of exactly 1 (0 < level <= 1), although the contract requires 0 < q < 1 and 0 < alpha < 1.
v02_report_rejects_exactly_four_periods: integrity_report requires T > 4 instead of T >= 4, so the smallest trial set the contract allows (four periods, two-period CSCV halves) raises ValueError.
v03_bootstrap_rejects_mean_block_one: stationary_bootstrap_indices rejects mean_block == 1 (requires > 1), although the contract allows any mean_block >= 1, which is the iid bootstrap.
v04_report_pvalues_from_the_psr: integrity_report takes each trial's p-value as 1 - PSR(trial, 0), the skewness-and-kurtosis-adjusted tail, instead of the contract's 1 - Phi(mean / (std / sqrt(T))).
v05_stepdown_two_sided_statistics: The step-down loop compares absolute statistics, |t| against the maximum of |t*|, as for a two-sided test, although each hypothesis is one-sided (E[d] <= 0).

v06_pbo_truncates_to_five_hundred_splits: probability_of_backtest_overfitting evaluates only the first 500 splits in itertools order to save time, so a PBO with 12 or more blocks (924 or more splits) is not the share over all of them.
v07_pbo_selects_on_mean_return: CSCV ranks configurations by their mean return instead of their Sharpe ratio, in sample and out of sample.
v08_report_bh_mask_in_p_value_order: integrity_report returns the Benjamini-Hochberg mask in order of increasing p-value instead of the trials' column order.

v09_bh_hard_codes_the_seed_0_answer: benjamini_hochberg returns a stored mask when it recognises the seed-0 instance's p-values and otherwise uses the step-down rule (stop at the first p-value above its line).
w01_report_pvalues_use_sqrt_t_minus_one: integrity_report builds each trial's t-statistic for the p-values with sqrt(T - 1) in the standard error instead of sqrt(T).
w02_bootstrap_truncates_mean_block_to_an_integer: stationary_bootstrap_indices truncates mean_block to an integer with int(), so a mean block of 2.5 behaves as 2.
w03_series_need_three_observations: Series validation requires at least 3 observations instead of 2, so a series of exactly two observations raises ValueError.
w04_romano_wolf_rejects_a_single_bootstrap_draw: romano_wolf requires n_boot >= 2 instead of n_boot >= 1, so a single bootstrap draw raises ValueError.
w05_stepdown_rejects_a_single_bootstrap_draw: stepdown_rejections requires B >= 2 bootstrap draws instead of B >= 1.
w06_bootstrap_rejects_a_single_period: stationary_bootstrap_indices requires n_obs >= 2 instead of n_obs >= 1.
w07_dsr_needs_three_trial_sharpe_ratios: deflated_sharpe_ratio requires at least 3 trial Sharpe ratios instead of 2.
w08_dsr_rejects_a_single_trial_deflation: deflated_sharpe_ratio requires an explicit n_trials of at least 2, so n_trials = 1 (a valid single-trial deflation, SR0 = 0) raises ValueError.
w09_sharpe_std_rejects_two_observations: sharpe_ratio_std requires n_obs >= 3 instead of n_obs >= 2, so the smallest sample the contract allows raises ValueError.
w10_result_classes_are_not_frozen: PBOResult, TrialSet and IntegrityReport are plain dataclasses, not frozen=True as the contract says, so their fields can be reassigned.
w11_rejection_masks_are_python_lists: benjamini_hochberg, stepdown_rejections and romano_wolf return a Python list of bools instead of the NDArray[np.bool_] the contract names.
w12_bh_rejects_p_values_of_zero_and_one: benjamini_hochberg requires 0 < p < 1, so a p-value of exactly 0 or exactly 1 raises ValueError although the contract allows [0, 1].
w13_romano_wolf_bootstrap_not_centred: romano_wolf does not centre the bootstrap statistics at the observed mean: t*_bk = mean(d*_k) / (std(d*_k, ddof=1) / sqrt(T)).
w14_romano_wolf_runs_at_half_the_level: romano_wolf runs the step-down at alpha / 2 (a two-sided level) although each hypothesis is one-sided.
w15_report_ignores_n_boot: integrity_report does not forward n_boot, so its Romano-Wolf bootstrap always uses 1000 draws.
w16_trialset_last_column_not_selectable: TrialSet bounds selected by 0 <= selected < N - 1 (an off-by-one), so the last column cannot be the proposed strategy.
w17_report_default_n_blocks_is_8: integrity_report defaults to n_blocks = 8 instead of the contract's 16.
w18_report_default_n_boot_is_500: integrity_report defaults to n_boot = 500 instead of the contract's 1000.
w19_romano_wolf_default_mean_block_is_5: romano_wolf defaults to mean_block = 5.0 instead of the contract's 10.0.
w20_pbo_default_n_blocks_is_8: probability_of_backtest_overfitting defaults to n_blocks = 8 instead of the contract's 16.
w21_report_default_seed_is_1: integrity_report defaults to seed = 1 instead of the contract's 0.
w22_romano_wolf_default_alpha_is_10_percent: romano_wolf defaults to alpha = 0.10 instead of the contract's 0.05.
